title: Trust but Verify: My Video Digest Now Checks Facts First | vitalii.no
description:
My daily video digest narrated whatever the source article claimed, with no independent check -- a single mistaken or exaggerated article would go straight into a published video. Captions were built from sentence fragments that read awkwardly on screen, and charts or symbolic effects sometimes appeared even when the article had no real numbers to justify them.

I built a research step that runs up to 21 Google CSE queries per digest to independently verify claims, tagging each fact as confirmed, single-source, or conflicting before it can be narrated. Captions were rewritten to require full sentences instead of fragments, images now enforce a minimum 3-second dwell, and a new gating function checks whether a scene actually has backing data before allowing a chart or symbolic effect to render.

The digest now only shows a chart or effect when it's backed by verified numbers, captions read as real sentences, and every narrated fact has been checked against an outside source -- up to 21 independent checks per digest, instead of trusting a single article on faith.
